As a general rule, I never take my vehicles to the dealership for repair unless it's warranty-related. It also doesn't help that the local dealers in my city have terrible reputations in the service department. The dealership isn't there to help you out. They''re there to simply make as much money as they can. Period.

Things like:

  • Oil changes
  • Brake jobs
  • Tire rotation
  • Minor tune-ups
  • First level diagnosis (eg. ECM reader)

Can all be done cheaply at home. Instead of paying $50-100 to have a code read on your car at the dealership - take it to PepBoys or buy a cheap code reader for $20 - 40.

There are tons of DIY videos on Youtube you can watch which will walk you through almost any mechanical or electrical situation.

Just be safe. If you're not sure, go to an independent mechanic for work you're not comfortable with.
Just to add, $3 OBDII reader from China + Torque app for all your code reading needs.

Instead of paying $50-100 to have a code read on your car at the dealership - take it to PepBoys or buy a cheap code reader for $20 - 40.

I would strongly caution to those not automotively inclined: Places like this can give you a code and give you a basic description, but may try to sell you a part instead of actually diagnosing the issue. Anyone can read a code, but diagnosing the proper issue and repairing the issue which is causing the code is where you will save the money. Throwing parts at a code until it goes away can be costly. For example, they could tell you that you have a code for a bad O2 sensor. The sensor may be perfectly fine, but there may be a problem with the wiring. Nine times out of ten, they will try to sell you an O2 sensor instead of suggesting a fix to the wiring.

I am all for DIY repairs, but if you are not comfortable or sure, ask someone knowledgeable. Ask us here. Sometimes DIY repairs lead to further, bigger repairs or, sometimes, you end up using a band-aid when you need major surgery.
